t: You're standing at St Anne and St Agnes, a church on Gresham Street in the City of London, close to the Barbican. It is an Anglican foundation, though from 1966 to 2013 it was let to a congregation of the Lutheran Church in Great Britain. The church was designed by Sir Christopher Wren, the architect given responsibility for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the Great Fire of 1666. His best-known work is St Paul's Cathedral on Ludgate Hill, finished in 1710, and this is one of the many smaller churches that came from the same rebuilding.
